en: What!? Is that what you were told? Ack. We must've gotten our signals crossed somewhere along the way.
Oh, is that not it?
Not quite. I actually came to talk to you today about how you became an idol.
Many of our readers are girls who dream of being famous one day, so your story can give them the hope they need to keep going!
Oh, all right.
But that's odd. I could've sworn I told your manager all about it.
I was told it would be about how I became an idol.
Yes, that's right! Many of our readers are girls who dream of being famous one day, so your story can give them the hope they need to keep going!
That sounds wonderful.
Great! And I'm so glad you've already been prepared. That should make things go a lot more smoothly.
Let's see. Was it the inside scoop on the idol business?
What!? Is that what you were told? Although, that topic does sound like it would be a big hit with our readers. Hmm.
All right, great!
Okay, let's get started. Now, I heard that you were scouted out in Okinawa?
They say you were just out shopping when somebody suddenly came up to you with an offer! So, what's your secret?
Do you have any tips for us on how to get noticed like you did?
Um. I guess there's just no tips to tell...?
I would suggest wearing a really cute outfit, and having your hair styled in an attractive way.
Ah, so being mindful of your appearance, is that it?
Yes, I think that might help catch the eye of a scout.
Is that what you did when you got discovered?
Well, actually, no. I didn't really do anything special.
I see. Then maybe focusing on your appearance doesn't help at all.
I'm sorry. I guess you're right.
I think the best thing to do is just be yourself and act natural. If you go overboard trying to catch the eye of a scout, it might look strange.
I see. I guess there really isn't any foolproof trick to getting noticed, huh?
I was only discovered by the president of my agency by chance. I guess it's just luck and being in the right place at the right time.
I'm sure our readers would have loved to hear there was some kind of trick to it, but I guess it is what it is.
Maybe if you have that certain "something," it shows even when you're just being yourself.
I would suggest smiling a lot, wherever you go. There's nothing more attractive than a beautiful smile.
But if you saw a girl walking down the street and smiling to herself, wouldn't you think there was something a little off?
Hmm. I guess you're right.
And when you got discovered, you weren't walking around smiling, were you?
Right... But I suppose it might be all right if you had a friend with you.
Yeah! Let's go with that!
All right, moving on. What was the very first job you had after becoming an idol?
And I don't mean dance lessons or anything like that. I mean a real, paying gig.
If I recall, it was being a guest assistant on a TV show. It was part of the promotion for the Princess League.
What kinds of things does a TV show assistant do?
I held signs and posters toward the camera. I basically just stood there and said nothing.
Seeing as you were already an idol, didn't you find that sort of thing a little humiliating?
Oh, was that question a little too hard to answer?
You know, if you don't say anything I'll have nothing to write about in my article.
I understood that's the way it had to be at first, because I hadn't proven myself yet.
So even idols have to toil in obscurity before they get better work, huh? That might be hard to hack for a lot of young people these days.
But not for someone who really, truly wants to be an idol.
Hm. I suppose it would be encouraging for our readers to know that even you had to earn your stripes.
It was a little humiliating, yes, but I let the humiliation fuel me into working that much harder.
Wow. You're resilient, aren't you?
Do you think so?
Oh yes, our readers will be very inspired by your story! No matter how exciting this business looks from the outside, it really is quite hard, isn't it?
I was just happy to be on TV. I never thought anything like that would ever happen to me!
Hehe, I can imagine! I think if I had a chance to be on TV, I'd grab it no matter what it was.
Now that you're getting so much attention on the Princess League, it's hard to believe there was ever a time like that for you!
Oh, there absolutely was!
Ooh, it must be so exciting to be an idol! I'm a little jealous!
All right. This next one is my last question. Do you have any regrets about becoming famous?
Well, the more famous you become, the harder it is to just be a regular girl, right?
You're probably discouraged from having romantic relationships, and people must recognize you wherever you go.
With these negative side effects, would you still recommend trying to become famous to our readers?
Look, Haruka-chan, you're not giving me anything at all to write my article on!
Yeah, I'm afraid "sorry" doesn't really help me out.
Oh, was that a tough question? Well, as someone our readers look up to and want to emulate, I was really hoping you'd answer.
Hmph. What a waste of a great question.
I believe you have to know what you're getting yourself into ahead of time, if you want to be famous.
Ah. Nobody can escape the price of fame, is that it?
While that may be true, I can't help but feel our readers will think that answer is a little too obvious.
They will?
You can worry about that after you get famous. If you try to think too far ahead, you might lose focus on what you should be doing now.
Ooh, that's right! Instead of just dreaming, it's important to try and move forward to make that dream come true, is that it?
Yes, I believe that's right.
Hehe. Well, it's definitely more convincing when you say it, Haruka-chan!
I wouldn't recommend it, no. You're right about it being hard to ever be a regular girl again. And it's not the kind of career that lasts.
Hey, wait a minute. If you say that, our readers are going to be really shocked and disappointed.
But that's how I honestly feel.
Well, if that's how you feel, I guess I can't expect you to lie.
All right, that's the end of the interview. Thank you very much for your time. It looks like I made the right choice!
My editor told me to go out and get an interview with one of my favorite idols.
And then I saw you on the Princess League, and instantly became a fan.
You did? How nice!
Hehe. And now that I've met you in person, you're just what I imagined! I guess I've got a good eye, right?
Well, thank you again. Remember, I'll be rooting for you! Best of luck!
Thanks so much!
All right, that's the end of the interview. Thank you very much for your time.
Of course. Thank you for coming.
To be honest, the interview wasn't as exciting as I hoped. But I think you've given me enough to work with.
Oh, I'm sorry. I hope so.
Yes, well, good luck to you. Maybe we can do this again sometime.
I'd like that. Thank you.
All right, that's the end of the interview. But... boy, the editor is really going to have my head over this one.
Yeah, well, nothing to do about it now. Thanks for your time.
"Sensual Gentleman" is a men's magazine that covers racy topics, but is not considered particularly vulgar.
Most of the readers are men in their thirties and forties. Magazines like these are probably their only source of information on idols.
It'd be terrific if you could win this segment of the market over, so do your best!
The interviewer will be Mizuguchi-san. He can be a little inappropriate at times, but the interview shouldn't last long. So hang in there!
The topic of the interview is advice for middle-aged men on how to be popular with younger women.
What they should do to get their attention, things like that.
(The interview is going to be about how middle-aged men can be popular with young women.)
(The readers are mostly men in their thirties and forties, so I should try to make my answers appeal to that audience.)
Hello. Is everything ready for today's interview?
Hey there. I'm Mizuguchi, from "Sensual Gentleman." Very nice to meet ya, Haruka-chan.
Thank you very much for coming.
Hehehe. Oh, boy! An interview with a young, new idol. I've been lookin' forward to this one, alright. You sure are a cute little thing, aren't ya?
Um, thank you.
No trouble, no trouble. So, 'bout the interview. Have ya been told what it's about?
What, they didn't tell ya nothin'? I thought I gave your manager the whole run-through.
Well, today's interview is about how middle-aged men can be popular with young ladies.
I see. All right.
But I dunno. I think your agency should be tryin' to run a much tighter ship.
Let's see. Was it how to have fun in a cabaret club?
What!? Why in the heck would I ask ya about that? That'd make no sense at all.
Oh. I'm very sorry.
Although, it might be kinda funny to see what you'd say...
Anyways. Today's interview is about how middle-aged men can be popular with the younger ladies.
But it is weird. They didn't tell ya anything at all? I thought I gave your manager the whole run-through.
I was told it would be about how middle-aged men could be popular with young women.
Yup! That's it in a nutshell! Can't beat hearin' it directly from the horse's mouth. Or in this case, a cute, young idol. Am I right?
Um, I'm not really sure.
'Course I'm right! Trust me. Okay, let's get the ball rollin'.
Let's see. Was it how to flirt with an idol?
Hmm. Can't say that's completely off the mark, but not many of our readers get the chance to come in contact with an idol.
So advice like that wouldn't do much for 'em, right?
Well, anyways. Today's interview is about how middle-aged men can be popular with the younger ladies.
Okay, let's get goin' then. Question one. In your eyes, what age do ya consider to be a  middle-aged man?
Sorry?
I wanna get your definition. When ya think of a middle-aged man, 'bout how old is he?
What, was that a tough one? Guess I'll just make somethin' up, then.
I would say anywhere between 25 and 60 is middle aged.
That so? Seems kinda young to me. You really think a 25-year-old guy is middle aged?
Well, I don't know if "middle aged" is the best term for it. I just mean, men in that age range aren't boys anymore. They're true, mature men.
That's a nice answer. With a positive comment about older men like that, this interview is gonna go over great.
Hey, I bet you'll even earn yourself some new fans.
I would say anywhere between 35 and 50 is middle aged.
Oh, yeah? So ya think a guy in his early 30s is still young, huh?
Yes, I do.
Well! With a liberal view like that on men's ages, I think this interview is gonna go great. Can't wait to see what else ya have to say.
I would say any man over 20 is no longer a young man.
Ouch! That's pretty harsh. In that case, you're talkin' about guys still in college.
Yes, I guess so.
A lotta our readers are gonna be shocked by that answer. But if that's what ya really think, guess we gotta put it in.
Okay. Next question. Let's imagine for a minute that you're over eighteen, and there's an older man ya like.
So he asks ya out on a late-night date. Where'd you like to go?
Late at night, you say?
Yeah, well, older men work during the daytime. Besides, guys might get some dirty looks if they're out with a younger woman during the day.
And they're adults after all, so of course they wanna go as far as they can, if possible.
So, what destination would make ya wanna say yes to a date?
What, are ya sayin' you wouldn't say yes?
Ouch, that's cold. A lot of our readers will be real disappointed. Ya could've at least given them an ounce of hope.
A private room in a restaurant. I guess there wouldn't be anything wrong with having a meal together.
A restaurant, huh? Not a bad idea. You're not old enough to drink yet, after all.
And I love going out to eat.
That's a pretty good suggestion. A restaurant sounds innocent enough that the guy might be able to hide his true intentions, too.
Yeah! I like that answer.
I like to sing, so a private karaoke room.
Well! But as a young lady, wouldn't ya be a little worried?
I mean, it is a private room and all. What if he suddenly makes a move?
'Course, I'd never do anythin' like that. I can tell ya one thing, though. I bet our readers are gonna like that answer of yours!
